activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Axel wanted to paint a rainbow. But he could not find his paints. He looked under his bed. He found only a red sock. He looked in his toy box. He found only a blue car.

Mama said, "We can make our own paint." Axel watched from his chair. Mama cut up a yellow lemon. She squeezed it into a cup. Then she cut a green apple. She squeezed that too.

Axel held his paper. Mama brushed the lemon juice on it. The paper looked plain and wet. "Wait," said Mama. They waited together. Axel watched and watched. Then the paper turned pink where the lemon had dried.

"More colors," said Axel. Mama squeezed a berry. The juice made red dots. Axel dipped his finger in the blue berry cup. He pressed it on the paper. He made a blue sun. He pressed green dots below it. Now his rainbow had red, blue, yellow and green. Axel held it up high. "I build a rainbow too," he said, pointing at his blocks.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Chloe went to the store with Dad. She wanted a toy pig. The pig sat high on a big shelf.

Chloe could not reach the pig. The shelf was too tall. She looked around the store. She saw red balloons by the door. She saw blue bins full of balls. She saw yellow signs that said "Toys" with a big arrow.

Chloe followed the yellow arrow. It pointed to a green step stool. The stool was heavy, so Dad helped her carry it. Chloe put the stool by the shelf. She climbed up one small step. She reached out her hand and grabbed the pig!

Dad laughed and hugged her. "Good looking, Chloe." On the way home, Chloe let the pig swing in the bag by her hand. The pig was pink and happy, just like her.

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
story:
Nathan went to the park with his dad. He saw a little turtle by the pond. The turtle was very small. "Can we take him home?" Nathan asked. Dad said, "Yes, he can be your first pet."

At home, Nathan put the turtle in a clean tank. The turtle sat very still. He did not walk. He did not eat. Nathan was sad. Then Dad filled the tank with warm water. The turtle popped out his little head. He began to swim! He munched a leaf too.

"Water makes him happy!" Nathan said. Nathan gave the turtle fresh water every day. He held his water cup tight so it would not spill. One morning, a big surprise waited in the tank. A baby turtle sat next to his pet! Nathan clapped his hands. "Now we have two!"

activity: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
knowledge_domain: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
story:
Charles sat at the little blue table. It was writing time at school! Miss Patel gave him a yellow pencil and paper.

"Today we write our names," she said.

Charles grabbed the pencil in his whole fist. He pushed hard. The pencil slipped. The letter C came out wobbly and fat, like a potato. Charles frowned at it.

Then he watched his friend Maya. She held her pencil with three fingers, like a little bird sitting on a stick. Her letters came out neat and small.

Charles tried it. He put three fingers on his pencil. He made a C. It was round like a moon! He made an H. He made an A. He made R, L, E, S.

The pencil did not slip anymore. The letters lined up in a row.

Miss Patel came to look. "Charles! You wrote your name!"

Charles held up the paper like a flag. "I can write it on my shoe box too," he said. "And on my cozy blanket. And on everything!"

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
story:
Elijah stood at the vet's desk. He held a small box. Inside was his new bunny, Pip.

"Pip looks grumpy," said Elijah. "Why is she grumpy?"

The vet smiled. "Maybe her tummy is empty."

Could that be it? Elijah wondered. He looked at Pip. Pip was chewing on the box corner.

"She chews because she is hungry!" said Elijah.

The vet gave Elijah a carrot. Elijah held it near the cage. Pip sniffed it. Then Pip munched and munched.

Elijah listened. The grumpy tummy sounds went quiet. "Her tummy is full now," said Elijah. "Food made the grumpy go away!"

At home, Elijah fed Pip each morning. Every morning, Pip munched. Every morning, Pip's tummy stayed quiet and happy.

"Are you hungry too, Pip?" Elijah asked.

Pip hopped to her carrot.

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
story:
Rosalie put on her short blue dress. Today was a big family party at Grandma's house. Grandma called everyone to the table. The candles were lit, and Grandpa said the blessing. Rosalie watched from her chair. The flames were little and bright.

After the blessing, Grandma made sweet tea. Rosalie wanted to help. Grandma held the cup, and Rosalie poured in the milk. The dark tea turned light brown. "Look, Grandma! I made it change!" she said. "Pour more," said Grandma. Rosalie poured more milk. The tea got even lighter.

Then it was time to spin the dreidel. Grandpa spun it first. It spun like a little wheel, then it fell down. Rosalie clapped. She spun it too. It wobbled and fell. "Again!" she called. The dreidel spun round and round on the table.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Austin went to the store with Mama. He wanted a big orange carrot. The carrots sat high on a shelf. Austin could not reach them. He jumped. He stood on his toes. Still too high.

"Can you help me, please?" Austin asked a store man. The man smiled. He reached up. He put a carrot in Austin's little hand. "Thank you," said Austin. The man gave him a sticker too. It was a shiny star.

Then Austin saw a tower of cans. It looked like a castle. He touched one can. The whole castle fell down. Boom, boom, boom. Cans rolled on the floor. "Sorry," said Austin, in a small voice.

The store man came back. "Let's build it again," he said. Austin handed him cans, one by one. The castle grew tall again. It was even taller now. Mama put the carrot in her bag. "Time to go home," she said.

Austin waved at the store man. "Bye-bye! Thank you!" The man waved back. Austin held Mama's hand. He looked at the carrot all the way to the car. "We will cook it," said Mama. Austin smiled big. "My carrot!"

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
story: Tonight was Diwali at Madeline's house. Grandma was making sweet dumplings in the kitchen. Madeline wanted to make one too. But every time she touched the dough, it fell apart. "It's too dry," Grandma did say. Grandma poured in a little milk. Madeline watched. The dry crumbs stuck together. The dough turned into a soft ball. "Can I try?" Madeline asked. Grandma gave her a small piece. Madeline pressed it flat. Then she pressed in a mold. She tapped it out. A little flower shape fell onto the tray. "I made one!" she said. Outside the window the sky looked stormy, but inside the lamps glowed. Grandpa lit the candles with a match, because only grown-ups do that. Madeline set her flower sweet by the lamp. She even left one for the tooth fairy cup where her loose tooth had been. "My shape made the tray look pretty," Madeline said. Grandma smiled and pointed at the tray full of flowers.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Sophia sat at the dinner table. The lamp was on. It made a warm circle of light.

"I want apple juice now," said Sophia.

"The juice is all gone," said Mama. "We drank it yesterday."

Sophia looked at her cup. It was empty. She turned it over. One drop fell out.

"Today we can buy more," said Mama. "We can go to the shop later."

"After dinner," said Papa. "First we eat."

Sophia ate her pasta. One spoon, two spoops, three spoons. Then she was done.

"Now?" she asked.

"Now we put on shoes," said Mama.

Sophia found her shoes. One shoe, two shoes. Her laces were messy. Mama helped tie them.

At the shop, Sophia held Mama's hand. They found the juice shelf. Sophia got to shake the bottle a little. Then she put it in the basket.

"Tomorrow we will have juice again," said Mama.

"And today too," said Sophia.

At home, Mama poured the juice. Sophia drank it all down.

"More now?" she asked.

"That's all for today," said Papa. "More tomorrow."

Sophia looked at the lamp. She yawned one big yawn.

"Tomorrow is after sleep," she said.

"Yes," said Mama. "Sleep now. Juice tomorrow."

activity: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
knowledge_domain: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
story:
Olivia wanted to paint a picture of a tree. She had red paint, yellow paint, and blue paint. But her tree was green, and she had no green paint. She stopped and looked at her cups. She had a big question in her head.

"Can I make green?" she asked Mama.

Mama sat down with her at the wooden table. "Try it," said Mama. "You have three colours."

Olivia dipped her brush in the blue paint. She made a blue spot on the paper. Then she dipped her brush in the yellow paint. She put yellow on top of the blue spot.

Olivia leaned close. The spot was turning green! Blue and yellow made green. She jumped up and down in her chair.

"My tree can be green now!" she said.

She painted a big green tree. She painted red apples on it. She painted a yellow sun above it.

Then she had an idea. She put red on top of the yellow sun. The red and yellow made orange! Olivia laughed and laughed.

"Mama, look! I made a new sun!"

The sun in her picture was orange, just like the one outside the window.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Mya wanted her red ball. It was hiding under the big block tower. She could see just a bit of red.

She began to take the blocks down. "One," she said. She put the block in the basket. "Two." Another block went in. "Three, four, five." The tower got smaller and smaller.

Her little brother Sam sat nearby. He dropped his teddy on the floor. Mya picked it up for him. Sam smiled and hugged the teddy tight.

She kept counting like the song on her toy radio. "Six, seven, eight." The tower was almost gone. "Nine." One block was left. Mya lifted it up high. "Ten!"

There was her red ball. She pushed it to Sam. Sam rolled it back. It bumped her toe. Mya laughed. "Your turn, Sam. That is your job now." Sam patted the ball with both little hands and pushed it again.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Blake wanted to be a mommy today. Her old teddy bear would be the baby. She wrapped him in a small towel. Then teddy fell on the floor. He bumped his head. "Oh no," said Blake. She gave teddy a soft pat. She put a bandage on his fuzzy ear.

Then teddy got hungry. Blake found a toy cup. She held it to teddy's mouth. She made a little slurping sound. Teddy felt better right away. "Good job drinking," said Blake.

Next Blake gave teddy a job. He would watch the paper flowers she had made. But a breeze came in the window. The flowers danced away across the rug! Teddy sat very still. Blake laughed and chased them. She taped one flower to teddy's paw. Now teddy could plant it in a tiny pot. "You are a garden bear now," said Blake. TeddBlake wanted to be a mommy today. Her old teddy bear would be the baby. She wrapped him in a soft towel. Then teddy slid off the chair. He bumped his fluffy head. "Oh no," said Blake.

She patted teddy's head. She gave him a pretend bandage. Then teddy got hungry. Blake filled a tiny cup with pretend milk. She held it to teddy's mouth. She made a little slurp sound for him. Teddy drank it all up.

Then Mommy called from the kitchen. Blake ran to see. Mommy was planting seeds in little pots. "Can teddy have one?" asked Blake. Mommy gave her the smallest pot. Blake pressed one seed into the dirt. She set teddy beside it. "Your job is to watch the seed," said Blake. Just then, teddy tipped over and his paw patted the dirt flat. "You helped plant it," said Blake. She clapped her hands.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Jacob wanted to ride the big slide. But the big slide was in the sun. It felt hot on his hand.

"Ouch," said Jacob. He pulled his hand back fast.

He looked at the small slide. That one sat in the shade. He touched it. It felt cold and smooth.

"The small slide is cold," said Jacob. "Can I go fast on a cold slide?"

"Try it and see," said Mom.

Jacob climbed up. He sat down. He went slow at first. Then he went fast, fast, fast.

"Wheee!" he shouted.

A boy named Sam ran over. "You went so fast! Can the small slide do that?"

"Watch me," said Jacob. He ran back up the steps.

Jacob slid down again. Sam put his hand on the big slide. "Ow, this one is hot," said Sam. "It's a smelly old slide, too."

"Come to my slide," said Jacob. "It's cold like ice cream."

Sam climbed up behind him. They went down one by one. Then they went down again and again.

At the end, Mom called, "Time for a snack! I brought you a gift."

The gift was two juice boxes, cold from the cooler. Jacob took a big sip. Then a small sip. The big sip was better.

"See," said Sam. "Big and cold wins."

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Jake ran to the block corner at school. "I will build a big tower!" he said. He stacked the red blocks up, up, up. His tummy felt bouncy and light. He was so excited.

Then Tom bumped the tower. The blocks fell down with a clatter. Jake's face got hot. His hands made tight fists. "My tower!" he yelled. Tom looked down at the floor. His eyes were sad and wet.

Jake saw Tom's sad face. His own fists got soft again. "It was an accident," Tom said, in a tiny voice. Jake took a deep breath. "Let's build it again," he said. "Together." Tom smiled a big smile. They stacked the blocks higher than before. Jake clapped his clean hands. "Teacher, look!" he called. "We can spell T-O-W-E-R too!" The teacher laughed and said, "You built a fine one." At circle time, Jake whispered to Tom, "Same team tomorrow?" Tom nodded, and patted the very top block.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
The bookmobile came to Edouard's street. It was a big van full of books. Edouard wanted a book about trucks. He wanted to keep it forever.

A lady inside gave him a card. It was his very own library card. He picked a truck book and held it tight. "This is mine now," he said.

"Not forever," the lady said kindly. "You can take it home. Then you bring it back on a certain day." She stamped a day inside the book. "Other kids want to read it too."

Edouard took the book home. He read it three times. He read it to his cat until the cat fell asleep. At bedtime he put the book by his door.

On the stamp day, he walked back to the van. He gave the book to the lady. Then she put it on the shelf. A girl picked it up right away.

Edouard watched her hug the book. His old book made a new girl happy. He smiled and picked out a book about trains.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Sara ran to the park with her bunny toy. She wanted to show everyone. But when she sat on the swing, her hands were empty. Bunny was gone!

"Bunny, where are you?" Sara looked by the slide. No bunny. She looked by the sandbox. No bunny. She looked under the bench. No bunny. A dog began to bark, bark, bark at a tall bush. Sara peeked in. The branches were thin and wavy. The wind blew and the thin branches moved. And there, when they moved, she saw something white!

"Bunny!" The wind stopped. The branches hung down and hid Bunny again. The wind blew once more. The branches moved, and Sara saw Bunny's soft ear. She reached in fast and pulled Bunny out. She hugged him tight.

Sara sat by the dog with a cup of juice. She gave Bunny a drink too, pretend juice, from her own cup. "Wind, thank you!" she said, and waved at the tree.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Mia was thirsty. She wanted cold milk from the big fridge. "Can I help?" she asked. "Yes," said Dad. "Get the small cup."

Mia looked at the cups. One was big. One was small. She took the small one. Dad poured the cold milk. "One cup, one splash," he said.

Mia watched Dad make tea. The kettle was fast. It huffed and puffed. Dad poured hot water. "Stay back," he said. "The tea is hot. Your milk is cold."

Mia touched her cup. Cold! She blew on Dad's mug. Would it cool down? Dad smiled. "The tea is slow to cool," he said. Mia sipped her milk. Then she held up her small cup next to Dad's big mug. "Small," she said. "Big!" Dad laughed and clinked his mug against her cup.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Scarlett wanted to find her favorite color at school. She looked at the big paint table. There were four cups of paint. One cup was red. One cup was blue. One cup was yellow. One cup was green.

"Which one is my favorite?" she asked. Her teacher smiled. "Try them and see," said Miss Ana. Scarlett dipped her brush in the red paint. She patted red dots on her paper. The red dots looked like little apples.

Next she painted a yellow sun. Then she painted a green grass hill. Last she painted a blue river. Then something surprising happened. Her blue river ran into her yellow sun. The paint mixed on the paper. The wet spot turned green!

Scarlett gasped. "The blue made green with the yellow!" she said. She tried it again. She patted blue on yellow. Green came back. "It does it every time," she said.

Miss Ana hung the painting on the wall. She put a little sign under it. The sign said "Scarlett's Colors." Tomás clapped for her. "I like your green," he said. Scarlett smiled big. Now she knew her favorite. It was green, the color she made herself.

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
story:
Zoe rode in the car with Daddy. They drove down the long road to the hospital. The sky was cloudy, but Zoe felt happy inside. Mama was at the hospital. A new baby was coming today.

Zoe wanted to give the baby a present. She had a little red hat. She put it in her small bag. She held the bag on her lap all the way.

At the hospital, Zoe saw Mama in a big bed. Mama held a bundle with a small face. "This is your baby brother," said Mama. The baby was asleep. His hands were very tiny.

Zoe wanted the baby to see the red hat. She held it up. The baby did not wake up. Then the baby made a little sound. He turned his head. His eyes opened. He saw the red hat! He reached out one small hand and grabbed it. The hat fell over his nose. Zoe laughed softly.

"He likes my present," Zoe whispered. The baby held the hat tight. Zoe patted his hand, very gently. "My hat, my baby," she said. Mama smiled at both of them.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Elena sat on her bed. It was windy outside. The wind made the curtain puff out. The curtain went swish, swish. Elena felt scared. She pulled the blanket up to her chin.

Then the curtain puffed again. It knocked her teddy off the sill. Ted fell on the floor with a soft thump. Elena looked down at him. His face looked sad in the dark. She did not want him to be sad. So she leaned over and picked him up. She held Ted close. Now she felt a little brave.

Mama came in with a little lamp. She set it on the table. The warm light made the room yellow. Elena felt happy. She showed Mama the curtain. "The wind did it," she said. Mama smiled. "Yes, the wind sent Ted flying." Elena laughed. That was silly. She hugged Ted tight.

Mama sat down and opened a picture book. It had a duck on a pond. Elena clapped her hands. She felt so excited. "Duck, duck!" she said. Mama read one page. Then another. Outside the wind went whoosh. But inside, Elena was warm and sleepy. She gave Ted a kiss on his nose. "Night night, Ted," she said.

activity: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
knowledge_domain: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
story:
Mason sat at Grandma's big table. He wanted to write his name. Grandma gave him a fat pencil. He grabbed it in his whole fist. He pushed and pushed. The letter M came out fat and wobbly. "It looks like a sleepy cat," said Grandma. Mason laughed. "Why does it look so funny?" he asked. "Try two fingers and your thumb," said Grandma. "Like this." She showed him her hand.

Mason tried it. He held the pencil with two fingers and his thumb. Then he turned the paper a little. He wrote M, A, S, O, N. Five letters! One, two, three, four, five. "I did it!" said Mason. "That's me!" Grandma clapped. The cat jumped on the table. Mason was not afraid. He showed the cat his name. "Look, cat. M for Mason," he said. The cat sniffed the pencil. "That's mine," said Mason.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Owen got to the playground early. The grass was still wet. The slide shone in the sun. Owen felt excited. He ran to the swing.

The swing was high. Owen felt scared. He held the chains tight. His feet did not reach the ground. "What if I fall?" he asked. "Hold on tight," said Mom. Owen held on. Mom pushed him soft and slow. Up he went. Down he came. Up and down, up and down. Soon Owen was not scared. Now he felt happy. He laughed out loud.

Then a big boy ran past. He bumped the swing. Owen fell off into the soft sand. He felt angry. His face got hot. He wanted to yell. But then he saw his ice cream cone on the ground. That made him sad too. Mom helped him up. She brushed off the sand. They sat on the bench together. Mom shared her own ice cream with him. Owen clapped his hands. He licked the sweet, cold cream. "Swings are hard," said Owen. "But ice cream is easy," said Mom. Owen laughed and licked again.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Matteo stood at the edge of the pool. The water was blue and thick with little waves. His teacher, Miss Ana, held out her hands.

"Hold my hands," she said. "We will practice kicking."

Matteo held on tight. He kicked one foot. He kicked the other foot. Small splashes popped up.

"I want to go fast like the big kids," Matteo said.

The big kids kicked their legs hard. They made big splashes. Then they moved through the water, fast fast fast. Matteo watched them. He saw their kicking. He saw their splashing. Then he saw them zoom.

Matteo kicked harder. His legs went up and down. Big splashes flew everywhere. One splash hit his own nose!

"Hey!" he shouted, and he laughed.

But then something happened. Matteo moved forward. The kicking pushed him along. He glided past Miss Ana's elbow.

"You did it!" MissAna called. "Kick, kick, kick!"

"Kick, kick, kick!" said Matteo. He kicked again. He moved again. He glided all the way to the wall.

Dad clapped from his chair. A little girl in a red hat pointed at Matteo.

"He goes fast," she said. Then she whispered to her own teacher, "I want to kick like that."

Matteo grabbed the wall. Water dripped from his chin. He turned around and shouted one more word.

"Again!"

activity: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
knowledge_domain: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
story:
Layla woke up in her bed. She was wide awake. "I want my bear shirt today," she said. She looked in her closet. She could not find it. "Mama, can I ask you something? Where is my bear shirt?"

Mama smiled. "First bath, then shirt," said Mama. Layla made a silly face. "A bath? In the morning?" Mama filled the tub. The water was warm. Layla splashed with her hands. The soap made bubbles. The bubbles made her skin slippery. Mama scrubbed her toes. "These toes smell like cheese," said Mama. Layla laughed. "Silly Mama. Toes smell like toes!"

Mama poured water on Layla's head. The bubbles ran down. All the soap went away. Layla looked at her arms. They were shiny and clean. "The bubbles went down the drain," said Layla. She waved at them. "Bye bye, bubbles."

Mama wrapped Layla in a big towel. The towel was soft. Layla's skin was warm and pink. Then Mama opened a drawer. "Look who was hiding here," said Mama. It was the bear shirt! It was folded under her pajamas all along. Layla pulled it on by herself. Her head popped out of the top. "I did it!" she said. Her heart felt happy and bouncy. She ran to the mirror. The bear on the shirt smiled at her. Layla smiled back. "Now I need socks," she said. "Bear socks."

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Evan wanted the big red truck. Ben had the big red truck. Evan grabbed it. Ben held on tight. The truck did not move.

Then the truck slipped. It fell on the floor. A wheel came off. Now nobody could play with it.

Miss Dana picked up the wheel. She put it back on. She held up the truck. "One truck," she said. "Two friends."

Evan looked at Ben. Ben looked at Evan. Could they both play? Evan had an idea. He would dig in the sand box. Ben could have the truck first. Then they could swap.

Ben drove the truck to the sand box. He scooped sand with it. Evan found a stick. He drew a road in the sand. The truck drove on the road.

Soon Ben held out the truck. "Your turn," he said. Evan took the wheel. Beep beep! The truck went down the road fast.

Then the bell rang. Time to clean up. Evan put the truck on the shelf. The last block went in the basket too. Ben waved. "Truck again tomorrow?"

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Wyatt wanted to build a big tower at school. He found some big blocks and some small blocks. He put the big blocks on the bottom. He put the small blocks on top.

The tower grew tall. Then Wyatt bumped it with his elbow. The tower was weak at the top. The small blocks fell down. The big blocks stayed up. Wyatt gasped. He looked at the floor. He looked at his teacher. "It fell," he said.

His teacher smiled. "Try again," she said. Wyatt built the tower once more. This time he made the bottom big and strong. He was slow and careful. He did not go fast. The tower stood tall.

Then it was snack time. The teacher gave Wyatt a cup of cold milk. Wyatt touched the cup. "Cold," he said. The teacher held a pot of hot soup. "That is hot," she said. "Only I touch it." Wyatt drank his cold milk. Then he ran back, fast, to his tower. It was still standing.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Alice wanted to make breakfast for her family. "I will make pancakes," she said. "Big ones."

First, Dad got out the bowl. Alice poured in the flour. Some flour puffed onto her nose. "You look like a snow girl," said Dad. Alice laughed and laughed.

Alice stirred the batter. She stirred and stirred. Then she poured a little circle onto the pan. Dad held the pan, because the pan was hot. But the batter did not spread out. It sat in one fat lump. "That is not a pancake," said Alice. "That is a pancake rock."

Dad tipped the bowl. The batter was thick and slow, like glue. Alice thought hard. Then she had an idea. "It needs milk," she said. She poured in some milk. She stirred again. Now the batter ran off the spoon, quick and smooth.

Dad poured the batter into the hot pan. This time it spread out wide. It made a big round pancake. "Look what the milk did," said Alice. "Runny batter makes a big pancake!"

The pancakes stacked up on a plate. Alice put two blueberries on the top one. They looked like two eyes. Mom came in and gasped. "A pancake is looking at me!" Mom said. Alice giggled and said, "Bathe it in syrup, Mom. It likes that."

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Nathan held Dad's hand on the ferry. "One brother, one mama, one papa, one Nathan," he said, counting his family. The boat was big and white. The water below was deep blue and splashing against the side.

Nathan leaned on the rail. The wind pushed his hair back. Then the big horn went, "Whooo!" The sound was so loud that a black bird flew up off the water. Nathan laughed. "The horn made the bird fly away!"

His little brother Sam began to cry. The horn had scared him. Mama gave Sam his soft red blanket. Sam hugged it and stopped crying. Nathan patted Sam's foot gently.

"Boat, water, bird, blanket," Nathan said, naming things. Then he saw something in the waves. A fish jumped up, quick and shiny, and slipped back down. "Mama, look!" said Nathan. Sam looked too, and pointed his small finger at the water.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Leon wanted to find his lost blue truck. He looked under his bed. He found a stuffed rabbit there instead. "Hello, rabbit," said Leon. He put the rabbit in his toy box with his blocks and his drum. Still no truck.

Leon followed a trail of crumbs across the kitchen floor. The crumbs led to the fridge. Inside, he saw fresh apples, milk and cheese. "Maybe the truck is hungry," he said. Daddy lifted the cheese. There sat the blue truck! A little mouse was sitting in the truck, holding a tiny crumb.

"The mouse was driving it," laughed Daddy. Leon made a small bed for the mouse from a sock. The mouse curled up in it. Leon tucked the truck in beside the sock. "Good night, drivers," he whispered.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Lea rode the bus with Gran. She held Gran's hand. They were going to the big library.

"I want a book about a cat," said Lea. "A snowy white cat!"

At the desk, a kind lady gave Lea a little card. It had Lea's own name on it. Lea picked a cat book. The lady put it in a bag.

"Can I keep it forever?" Lea asked.

"You take it home," said Gran. "Then we bring it back on Thursday. Other kids want to read it too."

Lea hugged the bag. At home, she read the cat book three times. The cat in the book felt soft in the pictures.

On Thursday, they rode the bus again. Lea gave the book back. Then she saw it. A boy took her cat book off the shelf. He sat down to read it.

"He is reading my book," said Lea. She smiled at Gran.

Gran smiled back. "Now you can pick a new one."

Lea ran to the shelf. She found a book about a big snowy bear. "This one!" said Lea.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Rose wanted her red crayon. It was lost. The sky was cloudy, so the house looked dim.

Rose looked with her eyes. No crayon under the table. She heard a tiny sound with her ears. Tippy tap. It came from the kitchen.

Rose smelled something sweet with her nose. Apples! Mama was cooking. "Come see," said Mama. Rose touched the floor with her hands as she crawled. There it was! The red crayon was by the fridge.

"Good finding," said Mama. She gave Rose a cool apple slice. Rose tasted it with her tongue. Sweet and yummy.

Rose sat down and colored a big red apple on her paper. "Just like the real one," said Mama.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Felix went to the library with his mama. He wanted a book about trucks. "Where are the truck books?" he asked.

"Let us look on the shelf," said the librarian. Her name was Miss Jo. Miss Jo pointed to a low shelf.

Felix saw books about animals first. A black cat sat on one cover. A cow and a pig sat on the next one. "These are all animals," said Felix.

Then he saw books about toys. A ball, a drum, and a teddy bear. He tapped the teddy bear book. Miss Jo nodded her head.

Then he saw books about foods. Apples, bread, and eggs. "Can books go in groups?" asked Felix.

"Yes," said Miss Jo. "Each shelf holds one group."

So Felix looked and looked. He found a shelf with trucks, cars, and buses. "Toys that go!" he said. He pulled out a big red truck book.

"Good finding," said Miss Jo. She showed him where the soft chairs were.

Felix sat down with mama. He turned the pages slowly. "Vroom," he said. "The truck is black on this page!"

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
story:
Charlie ran into the backyard with a box. Inside was a little bunny. "His name is Floppy!" said Charlie.

Floppy hopped out of the box. He began to chew the green grass. Then Floppy chewed a flower. The flower fell down. Charlie gasped. Floppy was hungry!

"Mom! Floppy needs food!" Charlie called. Mom came out with her phone. She looked at it. "We can get bunny food at the store," she said.

Charlie filled a bowl with water. Floppy drank it all up. Then Floppy ate some lettuce from Mom's hand. His tummy got round.

Mom put up a little fence. "This keeps Floppy safe," she said. Floppy hopped inside his new home.

Charlie clapped his hands. "Floppy lives here now!" he said. Floppy wiggled his nose at him.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Hunter wanted to help Dad cook lunch. But the grill was outside, so they went to the backyard. Hunter stayed close to Dad, like a little duck.

Dad put meat on the hot grill. Hunter saw smoke go up, up, up. The grill was hot. Hunter did not touch it. He could smell the yummy food. He put his hands behind his back and watched.

Then Hunter saw a sharp stick on the grass. He picked it up to poke a mud block. Dad said, "Let me take that, buddy." Dad held the stick for him, and Hunter poked gently. The mud block went squish. It made a messy, funny mark.

"Hot grill, sharp stick," said Hunter.

"Yes," said Dad. "And we stay together." Hunter held Dad's hand all the way to the door.

activity: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
knowledge_domain: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
story:
Sienna sat in a big chair at the doctor's office. "Will the shot hurt?" she asked. Mama held her hand. "Just a quick pinch," Mama said. "Then we go for ice cream."

The nurse wiped Sienna's arm with a cool, wet cotton ball. "Now squeeze Mama's hand," the nurse said. Sienna squeezed tight. She felt one quick pinch. Then it was done! A small bandage with a flower on it went on her arm.

At the ice cream shop, Sienna peeked under the bandage. Her arm had a tiny red dot. "Look, Mama. The dot is small," she said. Mama smiled and gave her a spoon. Sienna took a big bite of pink strawberry ice cream. Outside the window, the sky looked a little stormy, but inside it was warm and sweet. Sienna licked her spoon and said, "I was brave, and now I get ice cream."

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Leo ran to the play corner at school. A big cardboard box sat there. "It's a house!" said his friend Mia.

Leo peeked inside. The box was empty. No table. No baby. No plates. "Our house needs things," said Mia.

Leo looked around the room. He saw a rug on the floor. He rolled it up and carried it in. The rug turned the box floor soft and cozy. "One rug!" he said. He found a basket and a hat. "Two things for the baby!" He put the hat on a teddy bear. Now the bear was their baby.

Mia held the bear. "The baby is hungry," she said. Leo found a cup and a spoon. He stirred air in the cup. "Soup for you," he said kindly. The baby got a pretend hug too.

Then the baby started to cry, because Mia made a sad face. "Rock the baby," said Leo. He turned the bear side to side, slowly, slowly. The pretend crying stopped. Mia clapped her hands.

"My sister rocks her baby like that," said Leo. "At home, every day."

The teacher rang the bell. Time to clean up. But first, Leo gave the bear one more hug.

"Bye-bye, baby," said Leo. "See you tomorrow."

activity: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
knowledge_domain: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
story:
James ran into the writing club room. He wanted to write his name all by himself. "Today I will do it!" he said.

Ms. Rosa gave him a big pencil. James grabbed it with his whole fist. He pressed hard. The letters came out wobbly. His J looked like a squiggle worm.

"Try two fingers and a thumb," said Ms. Rosa. She showed him how. James held the pencil the new way. He made a slow, careful J. It popped onto the page, round and neat. Then a, then m, then e, then s.

"Look!" said James. "My name is full of letters!" He held up the paper. "That's me! I wrote me!"

Ms. Rosa clapped. "Write it again," she said. James smiled big and picked up the pencil.

activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
story:
Kayden ran to the kitchen. Lunch was on the table. It was a peanut butter sandwich, cut in little squares.

"Hands first," said Mom. She lifted Kayden up to the sink. She turned on the water. It was warm, not hot. Kayden put his hands under the fall of water. "Do you feel it splash?" Mom asked.

Mom gave him the soap. Kayden rubbed his palms together. Bubbles grew. One, two, bubbles. Three, four, bubbles. They counted all the way to twenty. The bubbles caught the light. Where did the dirt go? Into the bubbles, down the fall of water, away. Kayden looked at his hands. They were dry and shiny after the towel. The sandwich tasted good. Kayden looked at his clean fingers and smiled. "My hands are so bright!"

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Wyatt wanted a big garden in the backyard. Dad dug the dirt with a shovel. Wyatt dropped little seeds into the holes. He patted the dirt down with his hands. "Will you grow?" Wyatt asked the seeds.

Every morning Wyatt ran outside to look. The dirt stayed flat and brown. Then one morning, Wyatt saw green. Tiny leaves were pushing up! "Dad, come see!" he called. The seeds had turned into little plants.

Wyatt watered the plants with a spoon. One spoon for each plant. Some water dripped down into the dirt. The plants drank it up and grew taller. The leaves got big and wide. "What is hiding under there?" Wyatt wondered.

Soon Dad found something. He pulled hard on a green top. Up came a fat orange carrot! Wyatt laughed. The little seed had made a whole carrot. Dad washed it at the sink and cut it into rounds. Wyatt took a bite and began to chew. "My seed did that," said Wyatt. He ran back out to look at his garden.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Amira ran to the class window. A bird was making a nest in the tree. The nest had small red leaves in it. "A baby bird will come," said her friend Leo. Amira clapped her hands. She was so excited.

Then a big wind blew. The nest tipped over. The leaves fell down, down, down. The mother bird flew round and round. She looked sad, and Amira felt sad too. Leo stamped his foot. "I feel angry at the wind," he said.

"Let us help the bird," said Amira. She and Leo picked up the red leaves. Their teacher helped them put the leaves back in the tree. The wind blew again. Amira held on tight with her mittens. She was a little scared, but she did not let go. Then the mother bird came close. She sat on the nest. "Happy bird, happy me," said Amira. Leo smiled too.
